title: Integrated Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Security, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Ava Martinez
summary: This integrated guidance consolidates Redwood Inference's security controls and operational procedures across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response for security events, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineering, SRE, product security reviewers, and compliance owners.
body:
Overview:
This document defines the end-to-end security and compliance controls used by Redwood Inference to protect customer data and ensure regulatory evidence readiness. Sections cover: RBAC and authentication design, audit logging requirements and schema, data residency and retention schedules, secure SDLC controls for model and platform changes, incident response procedures for security incidents, compliance evidence collection and attestation workflows, and the risk & exceptions process.

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Fail-safe (deny) authentication and session policies.
- Immutable, tamper-evident audit trails.
- Clear ownership for controls and evidence.
- Measurable SLOs (latency/availability) are complemented by security SLAs.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Purpose: Provide fine-grained access controls across control plane, customer metadata, configuration APIs, and production runtimes.
Key controls:
- Identity source: Okta (SAML/OIDC) primary identity provider; SCIM for provisioning.
- Roles: admin, infra-engineer, svc-account, product-analyst, support-operator, compliance-reader.
- Resource scoping: roles are strictly scoped by resource-tag (customer-id, environment:prod/staging/dev, region:us/eu/apac).
- Privileged actions require MFA + time-limited approval for high-risk actions (delete-customer-data, change-encryption-keys, emergency-rollback).
- Service-to-service: mTLS between internal services; short-lived JWTs for external SDKs.
Implementation checklist:
- Enforce role separation in IAM mappings (Okta -> Redwood IAM).
- SCIM sync run daily; manual reconciliation weekly.
- Automated policies checked in CI: rbac-policies.yaml under infra repo.
Examples (pseudo YAML):
  - "roles: [\"support-operator\"]\n    resources: [\"/customer/123/*\"]\n    actions: [\"read:logs\", \"create:ticket\"]"
  - "roles: [\"infra-engineer\"]\n    resources: [\"/cluster/*\"]\n    actions: [\"deploy\", \"scale\", \"view:metrics\"]"
Ownership and SLOs:
- Owner: security (policy authoring) + eng-sre (enforcement).
- Audit target: 100% of privileged-role changes logged; weekly reconciliation target 99% coverage.

2) Audit Logging
Purpose: Ensure all security-relevant events are captured, stored immutably, and can be queried for investigations and regulatory evidence.
Minimum events to log:
- Authentication events (success/failure, MFA events).
- Role/permission changes (who, what, when, where).
- Customer data access (read/write/delete) including the principal and query scope.
- Key management actions (create/rotate/deactivate).
- Admin actions: deploy, rollback, config-change, emergency-override.
- Service-to-service trust changes (mTLS cert rotate).
Schema (required fields):
- timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, target_resource, target_id, outcome, source_ip, user_agent, request_id, trace_id
Storage and retention:
- Primary storage: WORM-enabled log store (vendor or self-hosted) with HMAC-signed bundles daily.
- Hot store (searchable): 90 days.
- Warm/cold archive: encrypted S3 with object locking, 7 years for high-sensitivity events (customer-data-access, key-management), 2 years for admin/audit events.
Alerting and monitoring:
- Alert on suspicious patterns: >10 failed logins from same IP in 10m, anomalous access to >5 customers in 1h by same principal, or any access to production data from an identity without a prod tag.
- Owners: eng-sre (alerting pipelines), security (investigation).

3) Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary:
- Customer chooses residency region at account creation (us/eu/apac). Data-at-rest and backups are stored in selected region unless explicit cross-border feature enabled.
- Metadata (non-sensitive) can be replicated for control-plane operations; customer plaintext data and embeddings are region-locked by default.
Retention schedules (minimum set):
- Short-lived cache (KV cache for inference): 24h by default, configurable down to 1h.
- Inference logs (per-request traces): hot 90d, archive 2y.
- Customer PII & training inputs: 30 days default unless contract specifies longer; retention-deletion run automated monthly.
- Audit evidence (see Audit Logging) for compliance: 7 years for enterprise contracts subject to regulation.
Cross-border transfer and export controls:
- All cross-region transfers require documented legal basis and customer opt-in.
- Data export tools produce an attestation bundle (hashes and manifest) for forensic validation.
Operational procedures for retention/deletion:
1. Ticket created in compliance tracker for retention exception.
2. Deletion job scheduled with preview output to owner team.
3. Owner approves and job runs; job emits deletion-report into evidence store.

4) Secure SDLC (applies to model onboarding, runtime changes, infra)
Objectives: Ensure changes to code, model artifacts, and infra are reviewed, tested, and provenance-tracked before reaching production.
Mandatory controls:
- Git workflow: protected branches, required PR reviews (2 reviewers for infra/model changes, 1 for docs), signed commits for release tags.
- CI gates: static analysis, dependency scanning (SCA), secret scanning, infrastructure plan diff checks.
- Model onboarding: model provenance manifest (source, license, hash, quantization steps), quality evals (perf/cost/regression), security review (data-snapshot analysis).
- Release process: staged canary deploys with automated canary metrics (latency, error-rate, model-quality metrics), rollback playbooks.
- Artifact signing & storage: all release artifacts signed and stored in immutable artifact repository.
SDLC evidence requirements:
- For each production change include: PR link, CI build id, signed artifact hash, deployment run id, canary metrics snapshot, and approver list.

5) Incident Response — Security Events
Scope: Security incidents that impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data or the control plane.
High-level process:
1. Detection & Triage: pager to sec-oncall; initial severity classification (S1: active data exfiltration, S2: potential exposure, S3: contained misconfiguration).
2. Containment: short-lived tokens, revoke sessions, isolate affected service, rotate keys where indicated.
3. Forensic capture: preserve relevant audit logs, take disk snapshots, capture volatile memory if needed.
4. Remediation & Recovery: apply fix, run remediation tests, and stage phased restore where needed.
5. Post-incident review: document timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-up actions (owner and due dates).
Communications:
- Internal: incident Slack channel (#sec-incident-<id>), daily standups until containment.
- External: customer comms template based on severity. Legal and PR notified for S1/S2.
Evidence preservation checklist (initial actions):
- Snapshot audit logs for time window +/- 2h.
- Export service traces and relevant request payloads to evidence store (encrypted).
- Record actions taken with request_id and operator.
Ownership & SLAs:
- Security on-call: initial triage within 15m for S1, 30m for S2.
- Eng-sre: containment plan within 60m for S1, 4h for S2.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose: Provide reproducible, auditable evidence for SOC/ISO/Customers.
Core workflows:
- Quarterly control attestations: owners submit evidence links to control evidence tracker by quarter-end.
- On-demand customer evidence requests: track request in privacy-portal, deliver evidence bundle (signed logs + attestation) within SLA based on contract (standard 30 days, expedited 5 business days for enterprise).
- Audit-runbook: pre-packaged audit bundles per control including screenshots, config exports, logs, and signed attestations.
Evidence storage and protection:
- Evidence store: encrypted S3 with MFA protect on deletion endpoints, retention per contract.
- Evidence metadata: manifest files with SHA256 hashes and signer identity.
Automation and templates:
- Evidence collection scripts (Python/Go) live in infra repo: scripts/evidence/collect_*
- Standard attestation template (signed by control owner) must accompany each bundle.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process
When a control cannot be implemented or a temporary deviation is required:
- Submit a Risk Exception Request (RER) in the governance tracker with: rationale, compensating controls, duration, mitigating steps, and approver list.
- Triage by risk committee (security + legal + affected product owner).
- Short-lived exceptions: approval window max 90 days, renewals require explicit evidence of mitigation progress.
- High-risk exceptions: require CTO and CISO signoff and monthly evidence updates.
Operational notes:
- All approved exceptions are tracked in exception register with automated reminders 14, 7, and 1 day before expiry.
- Exceptions create mandatory follow-up action and are included in internal audits.

Appendices
A: RBAC Change Playbook (example steps)
- Step 1: Create a change PR including policy diff.
- Step 2: Security review and approval (2 reviewers).
- Step 3: CI validation: policy linter, unit tests.
- Step 4: Apply to staging; smoke tests; 24h monitoring.
- Step 5: Apply to prod during maintenance window; verify audit logs generated.

B: Incident Response CLI snippets
- Revoke sessions for user_id: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/internal/sessions/revoke -d '{"user_id":"U123"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>'
- Snapshot logs range: python tools/snap_logs.py --start "2028-10-01T12:00:00Z" --end "2028-10-01T14:00:00Z" --out evidence/snap-<id>.tar.gz

C: Retention table (human-readable)
- KV cache: 24h (configurable)
- Inference traces: hot 90d / archive 2y
- PII & training inputs: default 30d (contract override)
- Audit evidence: 7y (enterprise) / 2y (standard)

D: Contact & ownership
- Security: security@redwood.company (oncall: #sec-oncall)
- Eng-SRE: sre-ops@redwood.company
- Compliance owner: Priya Rao (priya@redwood.company)
